### Comprehensive Prompt for Building the AILM.in AI Video and Image Creation Portfolio Website You are tasked with building a complete, high-converting portfolio website for an AI-powered digital agency called "AILM.in" (also branded as "AILM Digital Agency" in the footer). This website is a single-page application (SPA) with additional sub-pages handled via state management (no external routing library like React Router—use React state to switch views). The site promotes services like AI video ads, image-to-video conversions, affordable stock videos/images, storytelling videos, and more. It functions as a focused landing page to drive conversions (orders or inquiries) from cold traffic, emphasizing quick understanding, trust-building, and easy ordering. The tech stack must be: React.js (with TypeScript if possible), Tailwind CSS for styling (include custom animations like shimmer effects, neon colors, and pulsing dots), Lucide-react for icons (e.g., Play, ArrowRight, Users, Video, Image, Film, Check, X for disabled features, etc.). Use constants.tsx for data like pricing, testimonials, FAQs. Ensure mobile-first design, fast performance (optimize videos/images with lazy loading, but remove skeleton screens for videos—load them immediately upon section view). Handle errors like video playback issues (use tags with type="video/mp4", onError handlers) and cyclic object values (sanitize console logs). Browser tab title: "AILM - Turn Ideas into Visuals" (update dynamically for sub-pages, e.g., "AILM - About Us"). Build from scratch based on this detailed specification, derived from a full product requirements document (PRD) and iterative updates. Implement exactly as described—no additions or omissions. Output the complete code structure (App.tsx, components folder with modals/forms/pages, constants.tsx, index.html for Tailwind config/extensions like @keyframes for animations). #### Product Overview and Positioning - Product Name: AI Video Creator Portfolio (Web), branded as "AILM.in". - Hero Copy (Headline): "We Create Viral AI Videos, Images & Ad" (large, bold, high-tech font with neon accents). - Subheadline: "From AI video production to expert ad management—we handle the tech, you get the results." - Positioning: Service-oriented, not just a gallery—aim to convert visitors to orders/chats in <60 seconds. "Proof-first" design: Lead with showreel, social proof above the fold. - Primary Audience: Small businesses/eCommerce sellers (ads for Meta/TikTok/YouTube), creators/influencers (short-form content), agencies (quick fulfillment/white-label). - Business Goal: Maximize "request/order" conversions. - User Goals: Understand services in <10s, see examples quickly, know pricing/delivery, trust enough to act. - Success Metrics: Primary CTA clicks ("Start Order", WhatsApp/Book Call), secondary (portfolio views, form completions), quality (time-to-action, bounce rate, mobile conversions). - CRO Principles: One primary CTA repeated (sticky on mobile), authentic testimonials/logos, optimized videos (fast-loading, no autoplay—play on tap). #### User Journeys - Journey A (High Intent: "I need video ads now"): Land → See showreel/offer/price/delivery → Click "Order Now" → Select package → Upload assets → Pay → Confirmation. - Journey B (Medium Intent: Comparing): Land → Watch showreel → Scan proof/testimonials → View case studies (before/after) → Choose package or message WhatsApp. - Journey C (Low Intent: Unsure): Land → View use-cases (eCommerce, real estate, app promo) → Use "Brief Builder" form → Submit → Get quote. #### Information Architecture and Page Structure Single-page landing (home) + sub-pages (About Us, Shipping & Delivery, Refund Policy, Terms & Conditions, Contact Us). Use React state (e.g., currentPage) to switch views. Navigation: Logo ("AILM.in" with optional image logo), links (Home, Services—scroll to What We Create, Pricing—scroll to section, About, Contact). Footer with columns: Company (About Us, Terms & Conditions, Refund Policy, Shipping & Delivery), Services (quick links: AI Video Ads, AI Image Ads, Image to Video, Affordable Stock Video, Affordable Stock Image, Storytelling), Connect (social icons/links: Instagram https://www.instagram.com/ailmofficial, X https://x.com/AilmOfficial, LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/ailmofficial/, Facebook https://www.facebook.com/ailmofficial). Footer description: "AILM Digital Agency" above "Next-generation video/images & Ad production service for brands that need speed and quality. Powered by AI, refined by humans." Copyright: © 2026 AILM Digital Agency. Home Page Sections (vertical scroll): 1. **Hero (Above the Fold)**: Autoplay-muted loop showreel (5–12s, but no autoplay—play on tap), headline, subheadline, primary CTA "Start Your Order". Micro-trust row: "24h delivery", "Custom to your requirements", "Lifetime usage license", "Revisions included". Add "View Examples" button scrolling to "What We Create". Add "Accepting New Clients" badge with blinking green dot (animate-pulse on a green circle icon). 2. **Imagination Message (High-Tech Highlight, above See What's Possible)**: "We can bring your imagination into visuals. Just share the ideas of the video or script or images and we will convert them into a professional high quality assets." Styled boldly: Headline with moving gradient shimmer animation (@keyframes text-shimmer), keywords ("Ideas", "Script", "Images") in neon colors (cyan, fuchsia, yellow) with drop shadows. Glowing background blur, tech-grid overlay, "AI Processing Unit Ready" badge, tech dividers. Use Tailwind extensions for animations. 3. **See What's Possible (Trailer Video)**: Bold heading "Featured Showreel See What's Possible". Smaller landscape video frame (max-w-3xl). Video: ScreenPal embed
. No text overlay like "2024 Showreel". 4. **What We Create (Services Section)**: Bold headings for sub-sections. Each sub-section ends with a beautiful 2-line message: "We can create [section name] for your needs as your requirements in low cost." (e.g., stylized with italics/gradients). - **AI Video Ads**: Bold heading, 3x2 grid of 6 landscape videos (no autoplay, play on tap with InteractiveVideo component: overlay play button, error fallback "Video Unavailable"). Support Gumroad embed for checkout, pay deposit for high-ticket. - **Portfolio**: Filterable (Ads, Product, Image→Video, etc.), modals with description + CTA "Get this style". - **Analytics**: Track CTA clicks, views (but no implementation needed yet). - **Accessibility**: Video captions, contrast, keyboard nav. - **SEO**: Target keywords like "AI video ads", "image to video service". - **Trust/Safety**: Clear terms (commercial usage, revisions: "24 hours after assets received"). #### Sub-Pages Content - **About Us**: Story of AILM as hybrid AI + human agency for fast, quality creatives. - **Shipping & Delivery**: Digital delivery via Google Drive link for download. - **Refund Policy**: Strict no-refund: Deliver project, payment only on 100% satisfaction (watermarked drafts first). - **Terms & Conditions**: Usage, revisions, payments. - **Contact Us**: Form/email to support@ailm.in, WhatsApp/Calendly options. #### Assets and Customizations - All videos/images/embeds as listed above. - Remove unused sections (e.g., Example Videos, Documentary Style, Ai short Film, vertical videos). - Animations: Shimmer for messages, counting for stats, blinking green dot. - Colors: Neon green/yellow for arrows, cyan/fuchsia/yellow for highlights. - Make URL-based if possible (e.g., use window.location.hash for sub-pages like /about, but since state-based, simulate). Build and test for errors (e.g., video suitability with source tags, no cyclic logs). Provide full code ready for deployment.

**Identifying Core Needs**

I'm currently focused on the foundational needs of the "AILM.in" project, specifically determining the essential structure for an AI video and image portfolio website. I've pinpointed that it should be a Single Page Application with state-based routing. This should simplify the user experience and streamline development.


**Structuring Application Elements**

I'm now detailing the application structure, starting with `index.html` for setup and `metadata.json` for app info. I'm also planning out data structures in `types.ts`, like `Service`, `Testimonial`, and `Plan`, along with `PageState` enum. I'm focusing on defining core components and their data to facilitate smooth content flow and easy maintenance.


**Mapping Component Relationships**

I'm now mapping out component relationships within the application. I've broken down components into clear modules: `Header`, `Footer`, `Layout`, and specific UI elements like `InteractiveVideo` and `AnimatedCounter`. I'm starting to build out a hierarchy. I'm focusing on their data handling, using `Modal` and `OrderModal` for user interactions, and specific "Pages" for core content. I'm using `App.tsx` for state management, linking to the main `index.tsx`.


**Implementing UI Components**

I'm now focusing on specific UI elements and animations. I'm planning for custom animations in `index.html` like text-shimmer and pulse. For navigation, I will use an `activePage` state variable to manage page transitions. In terms of video handling, I will render ScreenPal embeds safely, after initial thoughts on dangerous methods. I will use a helper component for raw HTML snippets. I'm now working on the Hero section, aiming for a looping background video (a placeholder initially).


**Organizing Media and Interaction**

I'm now focusing on media organization and user interactions. I'm refining the Hero section, using a high-quality placeholder for the background and a separate ScreenPal embed later for "Featured Showreel." I'm planning CSS gradients and keyframes to enhance the visual. I'm also planning the Services grid layouts to be responsive, and using cover images with play buttons for InteractiveVideo.


**Translating Thoughts to Code**

I'm now deeply immersed in the coding phase. I've begun integrating Tailwind and custom styles in `index.html`, and handling responsive ScreenPal embeds. Within `App.tsx`, I've implemented a `currentView` state and `scrollTo` logic for smooth navigation. The `InteractiveVideo.tsx` component posed a challenge, but I've safely handled ScreenPal embeds by manually constructing the `iframe` src from the data-id. Finally, I've integrated icons from `lucide-react`. I'm now implementing neon color effects with CSS classes and managing browser tab titles. The next step is a final code review and assembly.


**Validating Project Assets**

I'm verifying that all URLs are integrated and that sub-pages have been created with essential content derived from the project prompt. Also, I've confirmed that the "Start Order" modal is functional and builds a `mailto` link. Custom animations have been added. I'm now constructing the XML output, with a facade pattern for the `InteractiveVideo` component. I will use a thumbnail with a play button as a placeholder. Clicking it will load the `iframe`.



**Constructing Embed Logic**

I'm now refining the `InteractiveVideo` component for seamless ScreenPal embed integration. I've switched to a direct iframe rendering approach in React, ensuring the video displays correctly within the Single Page Application. Also, after verification, I'm confident about using the `blogger.googleusercontent.com` URLs from the prompt, so I will incorporate them. I will now generate the code.

Create a professional, high-converting portfolio website for a digital agency named "AILM.in" that specializes in AI-powered video and image creation. The website should be a modern, single-page application built with React, TypeScript, and styled with Tailwind CSS.

**Core Features & Technology:**

2.  **Styling:** Tailwind CSS. The design should be fully responsive and adapt beautifully from mobile to desktop.
3.  **Navigation:** Implement a single-page application (SPA) style navigation. Use state to switch between different page components (Home, About, Contact, and legal pages) without full page reloads.
4.  **Data Management:** Store all static content (testimonials, pricing plans, service examples, FAQs, etc.) in a `constants.tsx` file to keep the main components clean. Define all necessary types in a `types.ts` file.
